newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Wheat Board says pool return rises.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Wheat Board says pool return rises.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday that the estimated return for wheat delivered to the 1996/97 pool had risen by A$4.00 a tonne in most cases.
The AWB said the estimated return for the Australian Standard White (ASW) poll was now A$192 a tonne fob (gross).
It said the rise for Australian Hard wheat was A$4.50 a tonne and the estimate for all grades of durum was now A$2.00 a tonne higher.
The estimate of the feed wheat pool remains unchanged.

"We're certainly seeing some benefit from the continued softness in the Australian dollar but primarily the rise reflects the benefits of our very early sales programme and marginally better prices than we had forecast," the AWB's general manager merchandising, Ron Storey, said.

"The really pleasing thing is that with more than half of this season's crop being graded into the premium or specialty grades most producers will be receiving in excess of the estimated A$192 for ASW," Storey said in a statement.
He said the AWB had currently shipped 5.5 million tonnes of new crop wheat and priced 10 million tonnes of its anticipated 18 million tonne export program for the year.
The next revision of pool equities will be announced on February 17 when the first estimated returns for 1997/98 will be included.
